quotes.quote: REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS
Date to be opened: 7/27/2026

The City of Providence Department of Public Works, Parking Administration Division, seeks competitive bids from qualified manufacturers and distributors for the furnishing and delivery of parking regulatory signs, parking sign posts, mounting hardware, parking control devices, and related materials on an as-needed basis under a firm fixed unit price requirements contract.
This solicitation will result in a Firm Fixed Unit Price, Blanket Requirements, Estimated Quantity Contract.

Award shall be made to the lowest responsive and responsible bidder based on the aggregate evaluated price and the bidder's demonstrated responsibility, delivery capability, product quality, warranty, references, and compliance with the specifications.

findings.title: Contract Type: Firm Fixed Unit Price, Blanket Requirements, Estimated Quantity Contract
findings.fact: The contract is a firm fixed unit price, blanket requirements, estimated quantity contract. Unit prices are fixed for the initial term and include all costs. The City does not guarantee minimum purchase quantities.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must carefully price each item to cover all costs and desired profit margin, as prices are fixed for the initial term and there is no guaranteed volume. The City may order in varying quantities, potentially low or zero, so the bidder bears the risk of low demand.
findings.action_recommendation: Conduct a thorough cost analysis to ensure unit prices are sufficient to cover all expenses and generate profit even with low order volumes. Consider including a contingency in pricing to mitigate the risk of low volume. Also, assess production capacity to handle potential large orders without incurring additional costs.

quotes.quote: This solicitation will result in a Firm Fixed Unit Price, Blanket Requirements, Estimated Quantity Contract.

findings.title: Contract Term and Renewal Options
findings.fact: The contract has a one-year base term with two optional one-year renewals, subject to satisfactory performance, funding availability, and mutual agreement. Renewal price adjustments are limited to the lesser of CPI-U increase or 3%.
findings.business_implication: The contract offers potential for a longer-term relationship (up to three years) but with limited ability to adjust prices for inflation or cost increases. The renewal is not guaranteed and depends on performance and funding.
findings.action_recommendation: Plan for a multi-year engagement by ensuring pricing is sustainable over the long term. Monitor costs and consider the 3% cap on price increases when setting initial prices. Maintain high performance standards to secure renewals. Also, prepare for the possibility of non-renewal by not overcommitting resources.

quotes.quote: One-year base term with two optional one-year renewals, subject to satisfactory performance, funding availability, and mutual agreement. Renewal price adjustments may be requested only during renewal periods and shall not exceed the lesser of the annual CPI-U increase or three percent, supported by documentation.

findings.action_recommendation: Ensure that the products offered are of high quality and durability to minimize warranty claims. Factor the cost of potential warranty claims into the pricing. Consider negotiating warranty terms or obtaining insurance to mitigate risk. Also, clearly document warranty procedures and ensure compliance with all requirements.

quotes.quote: Provide a minimum ten-year manufacturer's warranty covering reflectivity, delamination, peeling, cracking, corrosion, fading, adhesive failure, ink failure, and manufacturing defects.

findings.title: Bid Form Unit Prices
findings.fact: Bidders must provide unit prices for each sign item on the Bid Form.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must accurately price each specific sign type, as these prices will be used for evaluation and future orders. Incorrect pricing could lead to losses or loss of contract.
findings.action_recommendation: Carefully calculate the cost for each sign type, considering materials, labor, overhead, and profit. Ensure that the prices are competitive yet sufficient to cover costs. Double-check the bid form for accuracy before submission.

quotes.quote: Provide unit price for each sign: Item Unit Price ($) 12×18 Parking Sign Each 18×24 Parking Sign Each Handicap Sign Each Resident Permit Sign Each Tow Zone Sign Each Loading Zone Sign Each Temporary Parking Sign Each

findings.title: Additional Price Schedule
findings.fact: A separate schedule is required for sign posts, hardware, brackets, anchors, and portable devices.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must also provide pricing for ancillary items, which may be ordered separately. These prices will be part of the contract and must be competitive and profitable.
findings.action_recommendation: Develop a comprehensive pricing strategy for these additional items, ensuring they are priced appropriately to cover costs and generate profit. Consider bundling or volume discounts if applicable. Ensure that the pricing schedule is complete and accurate.

quotes.quote: Separate schedule for: Item Price ($) Sign Posts Hardware Brackets Anchors Portable Devices

findings.title: Optional Installation Pricing
findings.fact: Optional add/alternate installation pricing is required for various installation services.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must provide detailed unit prices for each installation service listed, as these may be used to determine the total cost of the contract. Failure to provide accurate pricing could lead to financial loss if the city exercises these options.
findings.action_recommendation: Carefully calculate and include competitive yet realistic unit prices for each installation service. Ensure all costs (labor, materials, overhead) are covered to avoid underpricing.

quotes.quote: Item Unit Price ($) Install 12" × 18" Sign on Existing Post Each Install 18" × 24" Sign on Existing Post Each Install New U-Channel Post and Sign Each Install New Square Tube Post and Sign Each Remove Existing Sign Each Remove Existing Post Each Relocate Existing Sign Each Install Breakaway System Each Emergency Service (Normal Business Hours) Hour Emergency Service (After Hours, Weekends & Holidays) Hour Two-Person Installation Crew Hour Traffic Control (if authorized) Day Concrete Foundation (if required) Each Mobilization (if authorized) Each

findings.title: Tax Exemption
findings.fact: Prices quoted must not include Federal Excise Taxes or Rhode Island Sales Tax as the City is exempt.
findings.business_implication: The bidder cannot include these taxes in their quoted prices, which may affect their profit margins. However, the bidder may be able to claim exemptions or credits for taxes paid on inputs.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure pricing excludes these taxes. Verify eligibility for tax exemptions and consult with a tax advisor to understand the financial impact and any required documentation.

quotes.quote: As the City of Providence is exempt from the payment of Federal Excise Taxes and Rhode Island Sales Tax, prices quoted are not to include these taxes.

findings.title: No Assignment Without Consent
findings.fact: Contractor is not permitted to assign or underlet the contract without prior written consent of the City Purchasing Director.
findings.business_implication: The bidder cannot transfer the contract or subcontract the work without explicit approval, limiting flexibility in resource management and potentially increasing risk if the bidder cannot perform.
findings.action_recommendation: Plan to perform the contract with own resources or obtain written consent from the City before any assignment or subcontracting. Ensure all subcontractors are vetted and approved in advance.

quotes.quote: The contractor will NOT be permitted to: a) assign or underlet the contract, or b) assign either legally or equitably any monies or any claim thereto without the previous written consent of the City Purchasing Director.

findings.title: Purchase Order Required
findings.fact: No goods should be delivered or work started without a Purchase Order.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must not commence work or deliver goods until a valid purchase order is received, which could delay project start and affect cash flow.
findings.action_recommendation: Establish a process to verify receipt of a purchase order before starting work. Communicate with the City to ensure timely issuance of purchase orders to avoid delays.

quotes.quote: No goods should be delivered, or work started without a Purchase Order.

findings.title: Financial Assurance Requirements
findings.fact: Bidders may be required to provide financial assurances such as certified checks, bid bonds, or performance and payment bonds, depending on which checkbox is checked in the bid terms.
findings.business_implication: The bidder may need to secure and provide financial assurances, which can tie up capital and increase costs. Failure to provide required assurances will result in bid rejection.
findings.action_recommendation: Review the bid terms to determine which financial assurances are required. Arrange for certified checks, bid bonds, or performance bonds as needed. Ensure all documentation is in order before bid submission.

quotes.quote: Financial assurances may be required in order to be a successful bidder for Commodity or Construction and Service contracts. If either of the first two checkboxes below is checked, the specified assurance must accompany a bid, or the bid will not be considered by the Board of Contract and Supply. The third checkbox indicates the lowest responsible bidder will be contacted and required to post a bond to be awarded the contract.
a)  A certified check for $      must be deposited with the City Clerk as a guarantee that the Contract will be signed and delivered by the bidder.

b)  A bid bond in the amount of       per centum (%) of the proposed total price, must be deposited with the City Clerk as a guarantee that the contract will be signed and delivered by the bidder; and the amount of such bid bond shall be retained for the use of the City as liquidated damages in case of default. Any person signing a bid bond as an attorney-in-fact shall include with the bid bond an original, or a photocopy or facsimile of an original, power of attorney.
c)  A performance and payment bond with a satisfactory surety company will be posted by the bidder in a sum equal to one hundred per centum (100%) of the awarded contract.
d)  No financial assurance is necessary for this item.

findings.title: Bid Validity and Price Firmness
findings.fact: Awards will be made within 90 days of bid opening, and all bid prices will be considered firm unless qualified otherwise. Requests for price increases will not be honored.
findings.business_implication: Bidders must be prepared to hold their quoted prices for at least 90 days, and any attempt to increase prices after bid submission will be rejected. This means that cost estimates must be accurate and account for potential market fluctuations during the validity period.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure that the bid price is based on current costs and includes a contingency for potential price increases in materials or labor during the 90-day validity period. Do not submit a bid with the expectation of negotiating price later.

quotes.quote: Awards will be made within nighty (90) days of bid opening. All bid prices will be considered firm, unless qualified otherwise. Requests for price increases will not be honored.

findings.title: Default and Delivery Terms
findings.fact: Failure to deliver within the time quoted or failure to meet specifications may result in default in accordance with the general specifications. Deliveries and/or completion are subject to strikes, lockouts, accidents, and Acts of God.
findings.business_implication: Bidders are at risk of being declared in default if they fail to deliver on time or meet specifications, which could lead to penalties or termination of the contract. However, certain unforeseeable events (strikes, lockouts, accidents, Acts of God) may excuse delays, but this is not guaranteed.
findings.action_recommendation: Carefully assess your ability to meet the delivery schedule and specifications before bidding. If there is any risk of delay, consider including a realistic delivery date and ensure you have contingency plans for potential disruptions. Document any force majeure events promptly if they occur.

quotes.quote: Failure to deliver within the time quoted or failure to meet specifications may result in default in accordance with the general specifications. It is agreed that deliveries and/or completion are subject to strikes, lockouts, accidents, and Acts of God.

findings.title: Worker's Compensation Compliance
findings.fact: Prior to commencing performance, the successful bidder must attest to compliance with the Rhode Island Worker's Compensation Act or submit a sworn affidavit if exempt.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must be in compliance with Rhode Island's worker's compensation insurance requirements or be able to prove exemption. Failure to provide the required attestation or affidavit could prevent the contract from being awarded or delay the start of work.
findings.action_recommendation: Verify your company's worker's compensation insurance coverage and ensure it meets Rhode Island requirements. If you are exempt, prepare the necessary sworn affidavit from a corporate officer. Have these documents ready to submit immediately upon award.

quotes.quote: Prior to commencing performance under the contract, the successful bidder shall attest to compliance with the provisions of the Rhode Island Worker’s Compensation Act, RIGL 28-29-1, et seq.  If exempt from compliance, the successful bidder shall submit a sworn Affidavit by a corporate officer to that effect, which shall accompany the signed contract.

findings.title: Certificate of Insurance
findings.fact: Prior to commencing performance, the successful bidder must submit a certificate of insurance in a form and amount satisfactory to the City.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must have adequate insurance coverage as determined by the City, and must provide proof of that coverage before starting work. Inadequate insurance could lead to disqualification or delay.
findings.action_recommendation: Review your current insurance policies to ensure they meet the City's requirements (e.g., general liability, auto, workers' comp). Obtain a certificate of insurance from your provider that names the City as an additional insured if required. Submit this certificate promptly upon request.

quotes.quote: Prior to commencing performance under the contract, the successful bidder shall, submit a certificate of insurance, in a form and in an amount satisfactory to the City.

findings.title: Bid Form Requirements
findings.fact: Bids must meet specifications, be in ink or typewritten, state prices in writing and figures, be totaled, and be signed in ink.
findings.business_implication: Bids that do not strictly follow the formatting and execution requirements may be rejected. This includes using ink or typewriting, providing prices in both written and numeric form, totaling the bid (unless unit price bid), and signing in ink. Non-compliance could lead to disqualification.
findings.action_recommendation: Carefully review the bid form instructions and ensure all blanks are completed. Write prices in both words and figures, total the bid if required, and sign the bid in ink. Double-check that all specifications are met or clearly note any exceptions. Have an authorized representative sign the bid.

quotes.quote: Bids must meet the attached specifications. Any exceptions or modifications must be noted and fully explained.
Bidder’s responses must be in ink or typewritten, and all blanks on the bid form should be completed.

The price or prices proposed should be stated both in WRITING and in FIGURES, and any proposal not so stated may be rejected. Contracts exceeding twelve months must specify annual costs for each year.

Bids SHOULD BE TOTALED so that the final cost is clearly stated (unless submitting a unit price bid), however each item should be priced individually. Do not group items. Awards may be made on the basis of total bid or by individual items.
All bids MUST BE SIGNED IN INK.

findings.title: Payment Terms: 60 Days
findings.fact: Invoices submitted to the City shall be payable sixty (60) days from the time of receipt by the City.
findings.business_implication: The bidder will have to wait at least 60 days after invoice submission to receive payment, which can strain cash flow, especially for small businesses or those with tight margins.
findings.action_recommendation: Assess cash flow impact and consider adjusting pricing or payment schedules to mitigate the delay. Ensure all required documentation is provided with invoices to avoid further delays.

quotes.quote: Invoices submitted to the City shall be payable sixty (60) days from the time of receipt by the City.

findings.title: No Interest on Overdue Invoices
findings.fact: The City shall not be obligated to pay interest on any overdue invoice or payment.
findings.business_implication: If the City delays payment beyond the 60-day term, the bidder has no recourse to claim interest, increasing the financial risk of late payments.
findings.action_recommendation: Factor in the risk of late payment without interest when pricing the contract. Consider building a contingency into the bid to cover potential delays.

quotes.quote: In no circumstances shall the City be obligated to pay or shall you be entitled to receive interest on any overdue invoice or payment.

findings.title: No Limitation on Liability
findings.fact: The City shall not subject itself to any contractual limitations on liability, and the City does not agree to limit your liability to the price of the Agreement or any other monetary limit.
findings.business_implication: The bidder's liability to the City is unlimited, meaning they could be held responsible for damages far exceeding the contract value, posing a significant financial risk.
findings.action_recommendation: Obtain comprehensive insurance coverage, including general liability and umbrella policies, to mitigate potential exposure. Consider consulting legal counsel to understand the full scope of liability.

quotes.quote: The City shall not subject itself to any contractual limitations on liability. The City shall have the time permitted within the applicable statute of limitations, and no less, to bring or assert any and all causes of action, suits, claims or demands the City may have arising out of, in connection with, or resulting from the performance of the work provided in the Agreement, and in no event does the City agree to limit your liability to the price of the Agreement or any other monetary limit.

findings.title: Indemnification Obligation
findings.fact: To the fullest extent permitted by law, you shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the City, its employees, officers, agents, and assigns from and against any and all claims, damages, losses, etc.
findings.business_implication: The bidder is required to defend and indemnify the City against all claims arising from the work, including legal fees, which could be substantial and not capped.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure robust risk management practices and adequate insurance to cover potential indemnification claims. Review the scope of indemnification with legal counsel to understand the extent of obligations.

quotes.quote: To the fullest extent permitted by law, you shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the City, its employees, officers, agents, and assigns from and against any and all claims, damages, losses, allegations, demands, actions, causes of action, suits, obligations, fines, penalties, judgments, liabilities, costs and expenses, including but not limited to attorneys’ fees, of any nature whatsoever arising out of, in connection with, or resulting from the performance of the work provided in the Agreement.

findings.title: Governing Law and Venue
findings.fact: The Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of Rhode Island, and any actions shall occur solely in the venue and jurisdiction of the State of Rhode Island or the federal court located in Rhode Island.
findings.business_implication: Any legal disputes must be resolved in Rhode Island courts, which may be inconvenient and costly for bidders located outside the state.
findings.action_recommendation: Consider the costs and logistics of potential litigation in Rhode Island when bidding. If possible, factor in travel and legal representation costs into the bid price.

quotes.quote: The Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of Rhode Island. You expressly submit yourself to and agree that any and all actions arising out of, in connection with, or resulting from the performance of the Agreement or relationship between the parties shall occur solely in the venue and jurisdiction of the State of Rhode Island or the federal court located in Rhode Island.

findings.title: No Dispute Resolution or Mandatory Arbitration
findings.fact: The City shall not be required to submit to dispute resolution or mandatory/binding arbitration.
findings.business_implication: The City retains the right to pursue litigation in court, and the bidder cannot compel arbitration or other alternative dispute resolution methods. This may lead to higher legal costs and longer resolution times for disputes.
findings.action_recommendation: Review internal dispute resolution policies and consider the potential for litigation. Ensure all contractual obligations are met to minimize disputes, and consult legal counsel on how to handle potential conflicts.

quotes.quote: With regard to any issues, claims, or controversies that may arise under this Agreement, the City shall not be required to submit to dispute resolution or mandatory/binding arbitration.

findings.title: Insurance Requirements
findings.fact: You shall maintain throughout the term of this Agreement the insurance coverage that is required by the RFP or, if none is required, insurance coverage that is considered in your industry to be commercially reasonable, and you agree to name the City as an additional insured on your general liability policy and on any umbrella policy you carry.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must secure and maintain adequate insurance coverage, including naming the City as an additional insured, which may increase insurance costs and administrative burden.
findings.action_recommendation: Review current insurance policies to ensure they meet the requirements and add the City as an additional insured. Obtain certificates of insurance and provide them to the City as required.

quotes.quote: You shall maintain throughout the term of this Agreement the insurance coverage that is required by the RFP or, if none is required in the RFP, insurance coverage that is considered in your industry to be commercially reasonable, and you agree to name the City as an additional insured on your general liability policy and on any umbrella policy you carry.

findings.title: MBE/WBE Participation Goal
findings.fact: The City of Providence’s goal of a combined MBE/WBE participation is 20% of the total bid value.
findings.business_implication: The bidder is expected to make a good faith effort to achieve a 20% MBE/WBE participation rate. Failure to meet this goal may require a waiver and could affect the bid evaluation.
findings.action_recommendation: Identify certified MBE/WBE firms and solicit their participation. Document all outreach efforts. If the goal cannot be met, submit a waiver request form to the MBE/WBE Outreach Director before bid submission.

quotes.quote: I acknowledge the City of Providence’s goal of a combined MBE/WBE participation is 20% of the total bid value.

findings.title: Apprentice Requirements
findings.fact: For construction projects valued at $100,000 or more, the contractor must utilize not less than 15% of total hours worked by apprentices.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must allocate at least 15% of total work hours to apprentices, which may require hiring and training apprentices, potentially affecting labor costs and scheduling.
findings.action_recommendation: Plan to meet the apprentice requirement by partnering with apprenticeship programs or hiring qualified apprentices. Ensure compliance reporting is submitted with payment requisitions.

quotes.quote: This ordinance outlines requirements for utilizing not less than 15% of total hours worked by apprentices.

findings.title: First Source Requirements
findings.fact: The First Source Ordinance outlines requirements for hiring Providence residents to work on the project.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must make efforts to hire Providence residents, which may impact recruitment strategies and workforce composition.
findings.action_recommendation: Develop a plan to recruit and hire Providence residents, possibly in coordination with the First Source office. Maintain records of hiring efforts and submit compliance reports with payment requisitions.

quotes.quote: This ordinance outlines requirements for hiring Providence residents to work on this project.

findings.title: Compliance Reporting Condition for Payment
findings.fact: Reporting efforts and progress towards achieving apprentice and First Source requirements is a condition for payment.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must ensure timely and accurate reporting of compliance with apprentice and First Source hiring requirements to avoid delays or non-payment. Failure to submit required reports with payment requisitions could result in withheld payments.
findings.action_recommendation: Establish a robust tracking and reporting system for apprentice and First Source hiring. Designate a compliance officer to prepare and submit required reports with each payment requisition. Attend the mandatory post-award meeting to understand specific reporting formats and procedures.

quotes.quote: The attention of prospective bidders is also called to the fact that reporting the efforts undertaken and progress towards achieving the requirements in this ordinance is a condition for payment.
The attention of prospective bidders is called to the fact that reporting the efforts undertaken and progress towards achieving the requirements in this ordinance is a condition for payment.

findings.title: Data Breach Notification and Liability
findings.fact: The contractor must comply with data protection laws, implement security measures, and notify the City within 24 hours of a breach, potentially incurring liability for breaches.
findings.business_implication: The contractor assumes significant responsibility for protecting confidential and personal information. A breach could lead to legal liability, financial penalties, and reputational damage. The 24-hour notification requirement demands a rapid response capability.
findings.action_recommendation: Implement comprehensive data security measures, including encryption, access controls, and employee training. Develop an incident response plan that ensures immediate detection and notification to the City within 24 hours. Review cyber insurance coverage to mitigate potential liabilities.

quotes.quote: For any Agreement involving the sharing or exchange of data involving potentially confidential and/or personal information, you shall comply with any and all state and/or federal laws or regulations applicable to confidential and/or personal information you receive from the City, including but not limited to the Rhode Island Identity Theft Protection Act, R.I. Gen. Laws § 11-49.3-1, during the term of the Agreement. You shall implement and maintain appropriate physical, technical, and administrative security measures for the protection of, and to prevent access to, use, or disclosure of, confidential and/or personal information. In the event of a breach of such information, you shall notify the City of such breach immediately, but in no event later than twenty-four (24) hours after discovery of such breach.

findings.title: Bid Bond Liquidated Damages
findings.fact: If a bid bond is required, the amount shall be retained as liquidated damages in case of default.
findings.business_implication: If the bidder is awarded the contract and fails to sign and deliver the contract, the bid bond amount will be forfeited as liquidated damages. This represents a financial risk that must be considered when bidding.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure that the bid is fully authorized and that the bidder has the capacity to enter into the contract if awarded. Review the bid bond amount and ensure it is acceptable. If there is any uncertainty about ability to perform, consider not bidding or seeking clarification.

quotes.quote: A bid bond in the amount of       per centum (%) of the proposed total price, must be deposited with the City Clerk as a guarantee that the contract will be signed and delivered by the bidder; and the amount of such bid bond shall be retained for the use of the City as liquidated damages in case of default.

findings.title: Performance and Payment Bond Requirement
findings.fact: If required, the contractor must post a performance and payment bond equal to 100% of the awarded contract.
findings.business_implication: The contractor must secure a performance and payment bond for the full contract value, which may involve additional costs and require a strong financial standing. Failure to provide the bond could result in loss of award.
findings.action_recommendation: Assess bonding capacity and associated costs early in the bidding process. Obtain quotes from surety companies and ensure the bond can be provided within the required timeframe. Maintain good financial records to facilitate bonding.

quotes.quote: A performance and payment bond with a satisfactory surety company will be posted by the bidder in a sum equal to one hundred per centum (100%) of the awarded contract.

findings.title: No Assignment Without Consent
findings.fact: The contractor cannot assign the contract without prior written consent; unauthorized assignment is voidable at the City's election.
findings.business_implication: The contractor cannot transfer its rights and obligations under the contract to another party without the City's prior written consent. Unauthorized assignment could result in the contract being voided, causing financial loss and legal complications.
findings.action_recommendation: If the contractor anticipates needing to assign the contract (e.g., due to merger, acquisition, or subcontracting), seek the City's written consent in advance. Ensure all subcontracting arrangements are structured to avoid assignment issues.

quotes.quote: You shall not assign your rights and obligations under this Agreement without the prior written consent of the City. Any assignment without prior written consent of the City shall be voidable at the election of the City.

findings.title: Compliance with Prevailing Wage and First Source
findings.fact: For construction contracts, the contractor must comply with prevailing wage laws and First Source hiring requirements; non-compliance may affect payment.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must ensure compliance with prevailing wage and First Source hiring requirements, as non-compliance can delay or prevent payment. This adds administrative burden and potential cost, especially if the contract involves construction work.
findings.action_recommendation: Review the contract scope to determine if construction work is included. If so, prepare to comply with R.I. Gen. Laws §§ 37-13-1 et seq. and Providence Code of Ordinances §§ 21-91 et seq. Establish processes for tracking and reporting compliance with each payment requisition, and attend any mandatory meetings to understand specific requirements.

quotes.quote: For contracts involving construction, alteration, and/or repair work, the provisions of applicable state labor law concerning payment of prevailing wage rates (R.I. Gen. Laws §§ 37-13-1 et seq., as amended) and the City’s First Source Ordinance (Providence Code of Ordinances §§ 21-91 et seq., as amended) apply.

The attention of prospective bidders is called to the fact that reporting the efforts undertaken and progress towards achieving the requirements in this ordinance is a condition for payment. Compliance reporting shall be submitted with any contract payment requisition, in a format to be specified by the City. This demonstration of compliance through such reports shall be a condition of the requisition for payment to be processed.

findings.title: Termination for Default in Delivery
findings.fact: Failure to deliver within the time quoted or failure to meet specifications may result in default in accordance with the general specifications.
findings.business_implication: The bidder faces risk of contract termination and potential liability if delivery deadlines or specifications are not met. This emphasizes the need for reliable supply chain and production capabilities.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure bid pricing includes adequate lead times and contingency plans. Clearly understand delivery schedules and specifications before bidding. Maintain open communication with the City if delays are anticipated, and consider including force majeure clauses where applicable.

quotes.quote: Failure to deliver within the time quoted or failure to meet specifications may result in default in accordance with the general specifications.

findings.title: Conflicting Statements on Renewal Price Adjustments
findings.fact: Section 4 states renewal price adjustments may be requested only during renewal periods and shall not exceed the lesser of CPI-U or three percent, but Section 3A states unit prices shall remain firm throughout the contract term except as otherwise provided for approved renewal-term price adjustments, which is consistent but could be ambiguous about the exact process.
findings.business_implication: The bidder may face uncertainty regarding the process for requesting price adjustments during renewal periods. This could lead to disputes or missed opportunities for price increases if not clearly understood.
findings.action_recommendation: Seek clarification from the City on the exact procedure for requesting renewal price adjustments, including documentation requirements and timing. Ensure that any price adjustment requests are made in accordance with the stated limits and supported by CPI-U data.

quotes.quote: Renewal price adjustments may be requested only during renewal periods and shall not exceed the lesser of the annual CPI-U increase or three percent, supported by documentation.
Except as otherwise provided for approved renewal-term price adjustments, unit prices shall remain firm throughout the contract term.
